# Abstract {#sec-abstract}




# Background {#sec-background}

Fantasy football has been the pinnacle of gambling, either by picking players to formulate a team, or to simply bet on another player. However, we aren't experts, so a lot of the issues that arise is from us not knowing the right players to choose, or the right thing to gamble on. Throughout my time being spent in a class where we deal with such, the psychology in statistics and human judgement, all of this can be encapsulated into a single idea.

## Research Question

The research question at hand may go both ways as an answer to such. But can we prove that our own R-code is a better, not certain, eliminator to the uncertainty?

## Hypothesis

I believe that our R-code can greatly eliminate the uncertainty. This is the only thing that drives us away from making those big bets (take this with a grain of salt, I am not an advisory for betting, or such betting). If we can get basic statistics on how players perform throughout their career, we can get a basic baseline to bet on.

However, this might be the one weakness that breaks this all, is where we can predict injuries, et cetera, but that will be a different conversation later.

## Justification

# Method {#sec-method}

All ideas were collected on behalf of the chapter selections by *Petersen*.

There are a few ideas that are combined into this. The first set of code collects all of the data for QBs, for simplicity, that ranges from their name, their total passing yards, touchdowns, interceptions, and their fantasy points. Mainly modeled from chapter 4.

The second idea was that I chose an easy QB, like Josh Allen, and predicted his 2025 season week by week (pretending that 2025 didn't happen yet), and took all of his previous seasons and predict what he will score for every week. Some code was changed from the textbook, but most of these ideas are all from the textbook itself, chapter 17.

With those ideas in mind, I added a statistical visualization to see the projected fantasy points for Josh Allen.

## Code

```{r}
qbs_from_2015_2024 <- player_stats_weekly %>%
  filter(
    position == "QB",
    season >= 2015,
    season <= 2024
  ) %>%
  select(
    player_id,
    player_display_name,
    season,
    completions,
    attempts,
    passing_yards,
    passing_tds,
    passing_interceptions,
    fantasyPoints
  )

joshAllen_2024 <- player_stats_seasonal %>%
  filter(
    player_display_name == "Josh Allen",
    position == "QB",
    season == 2024
  )

qb_season <- player_stats_seasonal %>%
  filter(
    position == "QB",
    season >= 2015,
    season <= 2024
  )

qb_week <- player_stats_weekly %>%
  filter(
    position == "QB",
    season >= 2015,
    season <= 2024
  )
```


```{r}
qb_week_prev_next <- qb_week %>%
  select(player_id, season, week, fantasyPoints) %>%
  rename(
    prev_week = week,
    prev_fantasyPoints = fantasyPoints
  ) %>%
  mutate(week = prev_week + 1) %>%
  left_join(
    qb_week %>%
      select(player_id, season, week, fantasyPoints),
    by = c("player_id", "season", "week")
  ) %>%
  rename(next_fantasyPoints = fantasyPoints) %>%
  filter(!is.na(next_fantasyPoints))

qb_week_model <- lm(
  next_fantasyPoints ~ prev_fantasyPoints,
  data = qb_week_prev_next
)

joshAllen_weekly_2024 <- player_stats_weekly %>%
  filter(
    player_display_name == "Josh Allen",
    position == "QB",
    season == 2024
  ) %>%
  arrange(week)

joshallen_prev_for_pred <- joshAllen_weekly_2024 %>%
  select(week, fantasyPoints) %>%
  rename(
    prev_week = week,
    prev_fantasyPoints = fantasyPoints
  ) %>%
  mutate(week = prev_week + 1) %>%
  inner_join(
    joshAllen_weekly_2024 %>% select(week),
    by = "week"
  )

joshallen_week_pred_mat <- predict(
  qb_week_model,
  newdata = data.frame(
    prev_fantasyPoints = ja_prev_for_pred$prev_fantasyPoints
  ),
  interval = "prediction",
  level = 0.95
)

joshallen_week_preds <- cbind(joshallen_prev_for_pred, joshallen_week_pred_mat)

joshallen_week_preds

joshAllen_2025_proj <- players_projections_weekly %>%
  filter(player_display_name == "Josh Allen",
         position == "QB",
         season == 2025)

joshAllen_2025_proj
```

## Statistical Visulization

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(
  data = joshallen_week_preds,
  mapping = aes(x = week, y = fit)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.2) +
  labs(
    x = "Week",
    y = "Predicted Fantasy Points",
    title = "Predicted Week-to-Week Fantasy Points for Josh Allen"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```
